newsitem.title: INDIA: India call flat, gilt yields steady in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: India call flat, gilt yields steady in dull trade.

text.p: Indian call money ended in the 0.10-0.50 percent range on the reporting Friday for banks, unchanged from the day's opening levels, dealers said.
They said four-day money was traded in the seven to 7.5 percent range while repos for the next fortnight were in the 10.0-10.5 percent range.
"The repos rates are clear indications that call money rates will be around 10 percent next fortnight," a dealer said.
Dealers said prices in the securities market were steady in listless trade.
"Market participants are worried about a tightening of liquidity as call money rates firm up," a dealer said. "They are not prepared to take any positions right now," one dealer said.
"The market is waiting to see the rsults of today's 91-day treasury bill auction and Tuesday's gilts auction," a dealer said. "These will give us some clue on the movement of interest rates."

The Reserve Bank of India conducts its weekly five billion rupee auction of 91-day treasury bills later on Friday. On Tuesday it will conduct a 20 billion rupee auction of six year government of India securities.
There was little activity in certificates of deposit or commercial papers, dealers said.
Rates on intercorporate deposits remained steady in the 17.0-19.0 percent range for top-rated borrowers, they said.
